title: You cannot pay the rent or mortgage this month
lede: The date is coming and the money is not there. Not late — absent. You have been avoiding the letters and the app, because opening them makes it real.

blocks.text: The date is coming and the money is not there. Not late — absent. You have been avoiding the letters and the app, because opening them makes it real.

items: Housing debt sits above almost everything else in priority, because the consequence is losing where you live. It gets paid before credit cards, phones, and buy-now-pay-later.
Avoidance is what turns a hard month into a legal process. Lenders and landlords have forbearance options that exist precisely for this, but almost all of them require you to make contact first.
Talking early puts you in the category of "cooperating borrower." Silence puts you in the category of "enforcement."
Nobody profits from evicting you if the alternative is a payment plan. Eviction is expensive, slow, and usually a last resort.

items.move: List every bill and rank it by consequence
items.detail: Housing, energy, council tax, food, transport to work first. Consumer credit last. This ranking is not moral — it is about what happens if you miss it.

items.move: Contact the landlord or lender before the due date
items.detail: Before, not after. Say the amount, the reason, and the date you can pay. A specific plan beats an apology.

items.move: Ask for the specific concession by name
items.detail: A payment holiday, a term extension, interest-only for three months, or a written arrears plan. Named requests get processed; vague pleas get logged.
A national debt charity, not a fee-charging company. They know concessions you have never heard of and they negotiate on your behalf.

items.move: Check what you are entitled to
items.detail: Housing support, hardship funds, council discretionary payments, employer hardship schemes. Enormous amounts go unclaimed.
Verbal forbearance vanishes with staff turnover, and a written plan is what protects you in any later hearing.

items.say: "I want to tell you before the date rather than after. I cannot cover the full amount on the 28th. I can pay £X then and the balance by the 15th. Can we agree that in writing?"
"Can you tell me what forbearance options are available — a payment plan, a temporary reduction, or a term extension?"
"I am trying to resolve this and I am asking for your arrears process in writing. I will respond to that."
Total income, total essential outgoings, every debt with amounts. Bring the numbers, not the feelings — they will handle the feelings too.

items: Ignoring the letters. Every stage of enforcement adds cost and removes options.
Taking a payday loan or a credit card cash advance to cover housing. It converts one problem into two.
Paying the loudest creditor rather than the most consequential one. Aggression is a collection tactic, not a priority order.
Paying a company that charges a fee to "manage your debt." The good services are free.
Leaving the property because you were told to verbally. Eviction is a legal process with defined steps.
Rebuild a one-month buffer before repaying anything optional. The buffer is what stops the next cycle.
Cancel the subscriptions you found while listing bills. That audit is usually worth real money.
Keep every letter and note every call with date, name, and outcome.
If the shortfall is structural rather than a one-off, deal with the structure: income, housing cost, or both. A plan cannot fix arithmetic.

limit: If you receive a court claim, a possession notice, or bailiff correspondence, get specialist housing advice immediately — there are usually defences and delays available, but only if you act inside the deadlines printed on the document.
